GPU: Optimize Throughput of a Large Number of Simple Threads
¡
Hundreds of Streaming Multiprocessors
(SM)s
¡
Each SM consists of:
¡
Processing units, e.g., INT32, FP32, FP64, etc.
¡
Simplified pipelines compared to CPU cores.
¡
Each unit executes specific instructions that are 
designed to specific computing precision.
¡
Warp Scheduler
¡
When deploy multiple threads, GPU packages a 
branch of threads into a warp.
¡
The scheduler decides which warp would run at one 
time slot, and these threads shard a register file.
¡
When one warp waits, schedule another ready warp.
¡
High-speed shared memory for intra-SM data 
exchange.
¡
Tensor core: accelerator for matrix operations.
Chip Organization

GPU: Optimize Throughput of a Large Number of Simple Threads
¡ A thread block is assigned to one SM
¡
Up to 8 blocks to each SM
¡
Fermi SM can take up to 1536 threads
¡ Could be 256 * 6 blocks
¡
Or 512 * 3 blocks, etc.
¡
Each block is divided into 32-thread warps
¡
Scheduling by the warp scheduler within a SM.
¡
Single Instruction, Multiple Threads (SIMT) 
abstraction
¡
Threads in a wrap should execution same 
codes/instructions.
¡
However, thread is allowed to execute different 
branches.

Hit: The requested memory block is 
found in the current cache level, with 
a valid tag match.
Hit Rate: Hits / Total Accesses
Cache Read/Write: Find the data on 
cache and then perform read/write
Miss: The requested memory block 
is not present in the current cache 
level, so it must be retrieved from the 
next lower level.
Miss Rate: 1 - Hit Rate
Miss Penalty: The additional time 
required to service a miss
